title: Measuring Validator and Sandboxed-Execution Coverage for LLM‑Generated NetOps Artifacts: A Paired Confirmatory Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) that measured the marginal detection benefit of adding sandboxed emulation to a deterministic validator for LLM-generated intent→configuration artifacts. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics using the declared/requested model "gpt-5-mini" (provider recorded as openai_responses) we evaluated Npairs = 720 confirmatory tasks. The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) flagged 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; the guarded pipeline (validator + sandboxed emulation) flagged 720/720 = 1.0. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Run accounting: model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair-stage call). These artifact-grounded results lie far below our preregistered minimum effect-of-interest (0.20). We report the preregistered design, exact quantitative outcomes, provider-call audit reconciliation, artifact-grounded interpretation for the negligible guarded benefit in this regime, and concise reproducibility pointers into the archived execution bundle.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate operator intent into device configuration and NetOps workflows. Operational deployment requires generated artifacts to satisfy syntactic correctness, workflow ordering, and higher‑order safety/policy constraints. A common mitigation architecture is generate→validate→(repair)→execute, sometimes augmented by sandboxed emulation to reveal runtime-only failures that static validators miss. Prior surveys and system reports document these workflow-centred mitigations and prototype evaluations [1]–[3], but provide limited large-scale paired measures of the marginal value added by sandboxed execution. Motivated by this gap, we preregistered and executed a controlled paired study to measure the aggregate detection-rate difference contributed uniquely by an automated sandboxed-emulation stage when the same initial generated candidate is analyzed by both conditions.

Research question and contributions. Our preregistered research question was: for synthetic intent→configuration tasks under shared_initial_candidate semantics, what is the paired detection-rate difference (guarded − baseline) between (A) a deterministic validator-only pipeline and (B) the same deterministic validator followed by automated sandboxed emulation? Contributions: (1) a machine-readable preregistration and faithful autonomous execution; (2) an artifact-grounded paired analysis on Npairs = 720 with complete accounting; (3) an explicit provider-call/audit reconciliation explaining stage-count asymmetries; (4) an artifact-grounded interpretation explaining a near-zero marginal effect and boundary conditions where guarded stages are likely to matter.
sections.related_work:
Workflow-centred mitigations and verification tools. Recent architectural reports and surveys emphasize that correctness in intent→configuration pipelines is multidimensional—syntactic parsing, command-ordering/workflow constraints, invariants (e.g., keep‑one‑uplink‑up), and dynamic runtime properties each require different V&V primitives. Tool-focused studies document the evolution and practical limits of static verifiers (Batfish and related configuration-analysis tooling) and motivate layering emulation for runtime behaviors that static rules miss [2]. Other recent agentic‑NetOps position and systems reports describe generate→validate→repair architectures and argue for combined validator+emulator workflows to raise operational assurance [1], while multimodal co‑pilot prototypes demonstrate the feasibility of exercising generated artifacts in emulated topologies [3].

Empirical positioning. Prior prototypes report heterogeneous gains from emulation: in some regimes a verifier alone catches most dangerous errors, while in others emulation uncovers subtle runtime failures not predicted by static rules. Those prior findings motivated our paired, shared_initial_candidate design that isolates only downstream guarded-stage effects (emulation observations or permitted repair invocations) rather than conflating them with generation variability.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and confirmatory design. We preregistered a paired-binary confirmatory design (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e). The primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline aggregated across confirmatory samples. The preregistered sample plan targeted Npairs = 720 (planned episodes = 1440) with a minimum effect-of-interest of 0.20 for power planning. Inclusion/exclusion rules, deterministic reseed policies for parser failures, multiplicity handling, and contamination controls were fixed before execution.

Task bank, topology templates, and vendor abstractions. Confirmatory items were generated deterministically from the intent_configuration_repair_v1 family and cover three abstracted vendor‑CLI families and three topology templates (leaf–spine, 3‑node service chain, triangle). Each task manifest specifies initial_state, expected_final_state, an explicit intent, a required_command_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and workflow policies (e.g., make-before-break). Inclusion required vendor‑parser acceptance after up to two deterministic reseeds; no irrecoverable parser exclusions occurred in the confirmatory run (complete_pair_count = 720).

Model and shared_initial_candidate enforcement. The declared/requested model was recorded as "gpt-5-mini" (provider: openai_responses) with the archived model configuration noting requested max_output_tokens = 2000 and temperature left null (no explicit client temperature). Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics exactly one sampled provider generation was obtained per pair and that identical candidate was provided to both downstream conditions; this isolates downstream guarded-stage effects by removing generation variability as a source of between-condition discordance.

Baseline validator and guarded pipeline. The baseline validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) performs vendor‑CLI syntactic parsing, per‑command canonicalization, sequence‑order checks against required_command_sequence, atomicity/workflow constraints, protected-interface invariants, group‑activity constraints, and final‑state conformance tests. The guarded pipeline runs the same validator and then executes the candidate in a sandboxed emulation harness that instantiates the declared topology and executes normalized CLI commands against vendor‑abstracted virtual devices. The emulation observes runtime behaviors (interface transitions, transient downtime, MTU/VLAN application effects, and topology-level reachability) and maps those observations to runtime-observation rules that can trigger additional detections beyond the static validator.

Provider-call audit fields: reconciliation and interpretation. The execution manifest and deterministic reconciliation archive provider-call audit fields intended to summarize model-call accounting; in our artifacts these fields must be interpreted as stage‑level call counts rather than per‑condition episode counts. Concretely: hosted_model_call_event_count = 721 equals the total provider calls observed (shared_initial_generation calls + repair calls). stage_counts enumerates calls by pipeline stage (e.g., shared_initial_generation = 720, repair = 1). condition_counts in the audit are a condensed per-stage label summary and in this run show entries such as "shared": 720 and "guarded": 1 because the single repair-stage call occurred during guarded-stage processing; this asymmetry does not contradict complete_pair_count = 720 because each pair contributed exactly one shared_initial_generation call (720) while repair-stage calls are optional and executed only when the repair policy invoked a model (1). Deterministic_reconciliation.json and the execution manifest provide the referenced artifact-grounded linkage between these audit fields and per-episode records. This explanation reconciles the apparent asymmetry in the audit counts without introducing new execution data.

Repair policy, missingness, and analysis plan. The preregistered repair policy allowed at most one repair-stage model invocation per task; the confirmatory execution used a conservative complete-pair handling (exclude irrecoverable technical pairs) and an exact McNemar two-sided test for the primary estimand, supplemented by a 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729). All per-episode artifacts, provider-call records, and reconciliation logs were archived as the canonical input to the paired-binary analysis executor.
sections.results:
Primary confirmatory counts and inference (artifact-grounded). Analysis artifacts report contingency counts: n11 = 719 (detected by both), n10 = 1 (guarded-only), n01 = 0 (baseline-only), n00 = 0 (neither). Marginal detection rates: baseline = 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; guarded = 720/720 = 1.0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884. Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. All numeric values are reproduced verbatim from the archived analysis artifacts (analysis/condition_summary.csv and analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) and analysis/results.json.

Provider-call accounting and discordant-pair attribution. Provider-call auditing and deterministic reconciliation record hosted_model_call_event_count = 721 with stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 720 and repair = 1. Because shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced, the single n10 discordant pair must arise from either (i) an emulation observation not encoded in the validator rules or (ii) the single recorded repair-stage invocation. The archived reconciliation links the discordant raw_results entry to the single repair-stage call; the confirmatory artifacts therefore localize the guarded-only detection to that documented repair-stage event (the raw_results.jsonl entry for the discordant pair contains the pair_id and repair_provider_trace fields that map the event to the repair invocation). The reconciliation artifact and per-episode traces permit independent auditors to inspect that mapping in the archived bundle.

Representative per-episode diagnostics. Representative scoring traces (execution/scoring/task-000001-*.json … task-000006-*.json) show validator_trace objects with normalized_configuration, validation_before/after, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, and violation_count = 0 for most pairs—illustrating a validator ceiling effect in this curated task bank.
sections.discussion:
Artifact-grounded interpretation. The negligible guarded-stage aggregate benefit observed (≈0.0014) is explained by three archive-supported factors: (1) validator ceiling effects—deterministic_netops_validator_v5 encodes the workflow patterns exercised by the curated tasks and achieved 719/720 coverage, leaving essentially no headroom for the emulator to add detections; (2) curated, parser‑validated inclusion reduced adversarial exposure and underrepresented runtime-only faults that emulation would otherwise reveal; (3) shared_initial_candidate semantics isolate downstream effects and limit discordance sources to guarded-stage observations or repair calls; in this run a single repair-stage invocation corresponds to the single guarded-only detection.

Operational implications. For operator regimes that employ a high-coverage static validator tailored to expected intent patterns and enforce parser validation, an always-on sandboxed emulation stage may yield negligible incremental detection return on effort for routine changes. Conversely, in noisy, adversarial, or broad multi‑vendor settings, emulation is more likely to surface runtime semantics and side effects beyond static rule coverage. Practical operator guidance (artifact-grounded): (a) invest in validator coverage for common, high‑throughput intents; (b) reserve guarded sandboxing for high‑risk or high‑impact changes; (c) use adversarial/fuzzing task banks to systematically identify validator gaps—the archived traces provide concrete seed cases for such efforts.

Limitations and scope. The finding is narrowly scoped to the preregistered task bank, validator implementation, the declared/requested model, and the shared_initial_candidate design. The study was powered a priori for a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed effect (~0.0014) is far below that sensitivity and must be interpreted as a near-zero result specific to this experimental regime, not as a general negative claim about guarded stages across all NetOps workflows. Emulation fidelity, broader vendor diversity, independent re‑generation strategies, and adversarial tasks remain open areas where guarded stages may confer larger benefits.
sections.conclusion:
We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study comparing a deterministic validator with the same validator augmented by sandboxed emulation on a curated synthetic intent→configuration task bank. Over 720 paired tasks the guarded pipeline produced a negligible aggregate detection gain (0.001388888888888884) with exact McNemar p = 1.0 and 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Provider-call reconciliation records model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair-stage call), and the single guarded-only detection is localized to that recorded repair-stage invocation in the archived per-episode artifacts. We interpret this narrow, artifact-grounded result as arising from validator ceiling effects and the curated task design; follow-up work should target adversarial and production-like task banks, expanded vendor diversity, multi-validator ensembles, and higher-fidelity emulation to identify regimes where guarded stages add substantive operational value.

Reproducibility pointers (compact). The canonical execution bundle archived by the run contains the execution manifest and per-episode raw_results, deterministic_reconciliation, model configuration, paired contingency tables, and representative scoring traces; these artifacts are the authoritative source for the numbers and mappings reported above and enable independent inspection of the single discordant episode and the repair-stage trace mentioned in the text.

limitations: Synthetic, parser-validated task bank and deterministic task generator produce limited ecological diversity and create a validator-ceiling effect; results may not generalize to noisier, adversarial, or production distributions.
Single declared/requested model family (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) limit generalizability across models and validator families.

Preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation reused across paired conditions) isolate guarded-stage contribution but remove between-condition generation variability; this design choice constrains discordance sources to downstream guarded-stage observations or repair calls.

Sandboxed-emulation fidelity relative to vendor/OS production behaviors and long-lived stateful interactions is limited by the emulation harness used; higher-fidelity emulators could change outcomes in other regimes.

Study power planning targeted a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed aggregate effect (~0.0014) lies far below that design sensitivity and should be interpreted as a narrowly scoped near-zero finding for this experimental regime rather than a general negative result for all NetOps workflows.
Provider-side nondeterminism and hidden caching remain residual uncertainties despite deterministic reconciliation procedures; these are documented in the reconcile artifacts archived with the run.
